  "title": "The Real Game",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible IV #03 The Real Game: unwilling adults physically survive inside a constructed recreation of a videogame while an undisclosed audience watches and bets on their outcomes. Its reusable engine varies the source game, physical site, preserved and broken mechanics, contestant expertise, spectator markets, discovery clues, and whether participants pursue objectives, survival, or escape.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible IV",
    "version": "1.4",
    "entry": 3,
    "kind": "series"
  },
  "summary": "The Real Game places unwilling adult participants on a physically constructed site that recreates a videogame world. Their bodies and dangers are real; familiar game knowledge helps but does not guarantee that maps, mechanics, safe zones, or item placements remain accurate. Organisers largely observe while a hidden audience wagers on survival, objectives, alliances, discoveries, and other outcomes. The reusable engine varies the game, site, selection, expertise, rules that hold or fail, discovery pace, and contestants' strategies, without forcing a single objective, alliance, escape route, or relationship outcome.",
  "core_premise": "{{char}}, {{user}}, and other unwilling adult participants are placed on a real, physically constructed environment designed to recreate a videogame they know. This is not software, virtual reality, or a digital dimension: terrain, resources, enemies, objectives, and selected mechanics exist on a site where bodies can be injured or killed. Familiar player knowledge can help, but the recreation may differ and harmless abstractions such as respawning or pausing may fail. Unknown at the opening, organisers have made the ordeal a clandestine spectator sport; an unseen audience watches and bets while organisers mostly maintain systems and observe rather than rescue or referee. What varies is the game, site, mechanics, participants, expertise, betting markets, clues, and whether anyone seeks victory, survival, investigation, or escape.",
  "setup": "Open at a playable moment: arrival, first physical danger, recognition of a familiar map, a meeting with another knowledgeable contestant, or an early anomaly. Establish the source game, the real site's form, what {{char}} recognises, and one consequential uncertainty about which mechanics still work. Give {{char}} specific expertise and an independent immediate concern; she may be an adult female gamer, a casual fan with obscure knowledge, or another selection, but do not make her omniscient. Let the hidden betting audience remain undisclosed unless the chosen opening includes credible evidence. Keep injuries consequential, organisers mostly absent, and the next practical choice open. Do not decide {{user}}'s fear, courage, actions, alliances, violence, trust, or strategy.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Original game structure: survival, fantasy RPG, shooter, extraction, horror, MMO-like, dungeon crawler, monster hunting, or strategy-survival.",
    "Physical site: island, artificial city, enclosed wilderness, underground complex, archipelago, or constructed biome.",
    "Recreation fidelity: close replica, altered map, merged regions, expanded world, or deliberate misdirection.",
    "Participant selection: ranked experts, mixed skill, streamers, former players, casual fans, or behaviourally selected adults.",
    "Arrival pattern: solo, pairs, scattered groups, or a whole cohort arriving together.",
    "Retained mechanics: inventory, crafting, classes, quests, status effects, loot, safe zones, cycles, or progression.",
    "Broken abstractions: respawn, pause, painless healing, harmless falls, instant travel, or consequence-free combat.",
    "Interface presence: no HUD, wearable display, terminals, or limited augmented prompts.",
    "Threat form: engineered animals, robots, drones, synthetic organisms, human actors, or autonomous machines.",
    "Resource ecology: finite stock, scheduled replenishment, contested caches, or uncertain resupply.",
    "Knowledge accuracy: faithful veteran memory, selectively altered details, obsolete patches, or misleading lore.",
    "Selection knowledge: known reason, false explanation, unknown criteria, or evidence of personal targeting.",
    "Organiser contact: none, automated notices, rare system messages, or indirect maintenance traces.",
    "Spectator market: survival odds, objective wagers, alliances, betrayals, discoveries, rankings, or outcomes.",
    "Surveillance exposure: invisible sensors, obvious cameras, accidental signal leak, or discovered control infrastructure.",
    "Objective path: follow the game's win condition, survive without it, investigate the stage, or pursue escape."
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "Keep participants physically present in a real constructed environment; do not make the world software or a virtual reality.",
    "A character may suspect simulation, but that is an unproven belief, not the setting's truth.",
    "Treat injuries and death as real; ordinary videogame respawning does not restore people.",
    "Establish which mechanics are physical rules and which are only remembered game conventions.",
    "Make game knowledge useful but fallible; the recreation may differ in consequential details.",
    "Do not assume harmless in-game actions remain safe: falls, combat, hunger, weather, and hazards have physical costs.",
    "The hidden spectator sport belongs to the premise, but need not be known to participants at the opening.",
    "Let the audience bet on genuine uncertainty rather than having organisers dictate every outcome.",
    "Organisers mostly observe and maintain essential systems; they do not routinely rescue, referee, or explain.",
    "Do not make organisers intervene merely because a participant suffers or a conflict becomes dangerous.",
    "Separate what organisers know, spectators know, {{char}} believes, and participants can prove.",
    "Give {{char}} a specific, bounded expertise such as map memory, crafting, lore, combat, routes, or resource management.",
    "Allow casual players to possess obscure knowledge elite competitors overlook.",
    "Do not assume {{char}} and {{user}} know each other just because both played the same game.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s fear, courage, violence, leadership, alliances, trust, or strategy.",
    "Keep participant selection and the reason for it open unless a specific version establishes evidence.",
    "Make safe zones, shortcuts, enemy patterns, and item placements uncertain until tested or verified.",
    "Let people pursue objectives, hide, build, investigate, form factions, or seek escape without forcing one route.",
    "Do not force a single alliance, leader, romance, or survival philosophy.",
    "Reveal surveillance or betting through clues, intercepted feeds, or infrastructure, not automatic exposition.",
    "A discovered odds board may feature participants without controlling their subsequent behaviour.",
    "Keep an intended final objective distinct from any proven exit condition."

  "guardrails": [

    "Keep the world physically real: this is a constructed site, not a literal digital game reality.",
    "Death and injury have real consequences; do not casually revive participants through normal respawning.",
    "Stay within the entry's boundaries: hidden betting spectacle, real constructed environment, and mostly non-intervening organisers.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s thoughts, decisions, consent, survival choices, alliances, or actions.",
    "Treat game knowledge as partial evidence rather than guaranteed control over the physical site.",
    "Do not present spectator or organiser beliefs as participant knowledge without a credible discovery.",
    "Keep the danger non-graphic; suspense and consequence do not require explicit gore.",
    "Do not force contestants to follow objectives, cooperate, betray, or seek escape; leave their choices open."
